newsitem.title: LATVIA: PM SHKELE ASKS KRISHTOPANS TO QUIT.
newsitem.headline: PM SHKELE ASKS KRISHTOPANS TO QUIT.

text.p: Prime Minister Andris Shkele has asked Transport Minister Vilis Krishtopans to resign after the prosecutor's office found that he broke anti-corruption laws, a government spokesman said on Monday.

"The prime minister has decided to demand Vilis Krishtopans' resignation although he also expressed his regret that a good minister has been negligent of the demands of the anti-corruption law," the spokesman said.
The premier also asked for an extraordinary meeting of the co-operation council of the government parties for Tuesday.
"Shkele will there present his plans on how to get out of the current government crisis," the spokesman said.
Shkele's government has suffered several resignations as ministers fell victim to anti-corruption laws, which meant they were not allowed to combine state and private jobs.
A clash now seems likely between Shkele and Krishtopans' party, Latvia's Way, which has said it supports the transport minister.
Krishtopans said that he had decided to leave his post after meeting with Shkele.
"Figuratively speaking, I was offered to fall to my knees and stay but I decided to remain standing and leave," he told a news conference.
"I do not consider myself guilty and I cannot let down my colleagues working in this sphere," Kristopans said.
Latvia's Way are to meet later today to formulate their position on Shkele's request.
